title: India's New Army Chief Has a Five-Letter Plan to Reshape the World's Largest Volunteer Force
excerpt: General Dhiraj Seth, the first officer from the Armoured Corps to lead the Army in nearly three decades, has unveiled a 'VIJAY' framework centred on AI, drones and soldier welfare.
body:
India's military entered a new chapter on Tuesday when General Dhiraj Seth assumed command as the 31st Chief of the Army Staff, succeeding General Upendra Dwivedi at a time when the 1.4-million-strong force is undergoing its most ambitious transformation in decades.

General Seth — the first officer from the Armoured Corps to hold the top post since General Shankar Roychowdhury retired in 1997 — wasted no time in signalling the direction of his tenure. In his first address after receiving a guard of honour on the lawns of South Block, he laid out a strategic vision distilled into the acronym **VIJAY**: Vigilance and Readiness, Innovation and Transformation, Jointness and Integration, Aatmanirbharta (self-reliance), and Yoddha First — placing the soldier at the heart of the force's evolution.

"The Indian Army will continue evolving into a future-ready force capable of responding effectively to increasingly complex security challenges," General Seth said.

## A Military Family, a Modern General

In a moment that captured the emotional weight of the ceremony, General Seth saluted and then touched the feet of his father, Lieutenant General K.M. Seth (retired), who himself once commanded two strike corps and served as the Adjutant General. His younger brother, Rear Admiral Ravnish Seth, is a serving flag officer in the Indian Navy — making the Seth family one of very few in India with two siblings holding star-rank commands across different services.

Commissioned into the Armoured Corps in December 1986 after passing out of the National Defence Academy in Khadakwasla, General Seth brings nearly four decades of service spanning desert warfare on the western frontier, counter-insurgency operations in Jammu & Kashmir, and high-level capability development at Army Headquarters. As a Lieutenant General, he commanded the Sudarshan Chakra Corps — one of the Army's premier strike formations — and later served as General Officer Commanding, Delhi Area.

## The VIJAY Blueprint

Each letter of General Seth's framework maps to a pressing strategic priority:

**Vigilance and Readiness** reflects the need for 24/7 preparedness along India's contested borders — the 3,488-km Line of Actual Control with China and the active Line of Control with Pakistan. Under his predecessor, the Army invested in theatre-level intelligence hubs and rapid-deployment units; General Seth's emphasis suggests an acceleration.

**Innovation and Transformation** covers the Army's push into artificial intelligence, unmanned systems, and cyber warfare. India is fielding AI-assisted surveillance on the LAC and testing indigenous drone swarms for use in high-altitude operations. General Seth's armoured corps background also signals a modernisation push for India's mechanised forces.

**Jointness and Integration** speaks directly to the integrated theatre command structure that has been under discussion since 2019 but has yet to materialise. General Dwivedi, in his farewell, stressed that future conflicts would demand far greater jointness among the three services — a baton General Seth is expected to carry forward.

**Aatmanirbharta** aligns with the government's push to source 75% of defence equipment domestically by 2030. India's indigenous Tejas light combat aircraft, the Arjun main battle tank, and a new-generation battle management system are all part of this programme.

**Yoddha First** — literally "warrior first" — signals a renewed focus on soldier welfare: pay, housing, mental health, and the combat gear that troops carry into the field. The Indian Army has faced criticism in recent years over delays in modernising personal equipment for troops deployed in extreme conditions.

## What It Means for NRIs and the Diaspora

For the Indian diaspora, the leadership change is significant beyond symbolism. General Seth's tenure will coincide with a deepening India-U.S. defence partnership — including the recently cleared $482 million Pentagon support package for India's Apache and M777 fleets — and the Japan-India defence corridor that Prime Minister Takaichi's visit is expected to formalise.

Indian Americans working in defence technology and dual-use sectors may see expanded collaboration pathways as the VIJAY framework's "Innovation" pillar drives partnerships with Western defence firms. The "Aatmanirbharta" pillar, meanwhile, creates opportunities for diaspora entrepreneurs and investors in India's growing private defence manufacturing ecosystem, which the government has opened to 100% foreign direct investment through the automatic route.

General Seth's tenure is expected to run until August 2028, during which he will oversee a force navigating the twin pressures of great-power competition on its northern borders and an accelerating technological revolution in the character of warfare itself.

*Sources: Press Information Bureau, The Hindu BusinessLine, Reuters, ANI*
